newsitem.title: USA: NYC axes commercial rent tax for Manhattan south.
newsitem.headline: NYC axes commercial rent tax for Manhattan south.

text.p: New York City Mayor Rudolph Giuliani on Monday signed legislation ending the unpopular commercial rent tax for more than 9,200 firms located south of 96 the street in Manhattan.

The bill ends the tax for businesses in that area that pay rents of less than $100,000 for the fiscal year that started on July 1. As a result, the city was expected to forgo about $30 million of revenues.

The new law also creates tax credits of varying amounts for commercial tenants with base rents that run from $100,000 to $139,000, a step city officials said would benefit another 3,400 more Manhattan businesses.

Giuliani called the bill an important element in his Administration's comprehensive tax reduction and reform program. The commercial rent tax has been phased out over several years, and Giuliani often cites this as an example of how he has changed the city's attitude by making it more friendly to business.

Separately, the Republican mayor, who stands for re-election in November, signed a bill that creates a Gambling Control Commission to license and regulate shipboard gambling businesses that are run from New York City docks.

Amendments to federal laws recently legalized gambling so-called cruises to nowhere Giuliani said. He said he likely would approve the measure several weeks ago after it was sent to him by the City Council, but added that he expected the gambling ships to test the restrictions in court.

Under the new law, employees of the cruises and vendors who are hired will be required to register with the new commission and get certificates of approval. City Council sponsors said the measure would help ensure safety on the sea and discourage criminals from controlling the trade.
